problem: The lead says the subtraction of TS leaves "the part that can become work". For G at constant pressure the usable part is only the non-PV (useful) work; total work including PΔV belongs to A. A student can read the lead and think −ΔG is the total work.
fix: Say: at fixed T and V, −ΔA is the maximum total work obtainable; at fixed T and P, −ΔG is the maximum non-PV useful work obtainable, because the PΔV part is already spent pushing the atmosphere.

where: Section 3, last paragraph, and Exam trap 5
problem: ΔA = ΔU − TΔS and ΔG = ΔH − TΔS are written without saying they hold only when the temperature is constant. At constant T they are correct; in general the relation is ΔA = ΔU − Δ(TS).
fix: Write "at constant T: ΔA = ΔU − TΔS and ΔG = ΔH − TΔS", and keep the point that they differ whenever ΔU or Δ(PV) is not zero.

problem: The chapter never states plainly that A and G are state functions and extensive, so they add up over phases and scale with the amount of material. Students meeting ΔG of reaction mixtures later need this.
fix: Add one sentence: A and G are state functions and extensive; for a mixture G = Σ nᵢ μᵢ, and per mole they are intensive.

problem: "Both have units of J, or J/mol per mole" is garbled wording; "J/mol per mole" means nothing.
fix: "Both have units of J; expressed per mole they are J/mol."

problem: The Gibbs-Helmholtz equation is dropped in with no derivation or use, then the Beyond box tells the student to "search next for Gibbs-Helmholtz equation" as if it were new. Quiz Q8 tests it, so the treatment is thin for a 3-mark question.
fix: Either derive it in one line from d(G/T) = −H dT/T² (or from G = H − TS with the dG expression), or move it out of Section 2 and delete it from the Beyond list.
